# `engine/testdata/` — golden fixtures

Everything in this directory is **generated by the TypeScript reference engine and
committed**. Nothing here is written by hand, and nothing here is written by the
C++ engine.

- Generator: `packages/engine/test/golden-traces.test.ts`
- Regenerate: `npm run export:golden`
- Drift gate: the same test regenerates every fixture in memory on each normal run
  and fails on the first differing byte, in both `npm run verify` and CI.

If a fixture and the generator disagree, one of the two engines changed. That is
the point: this directory is where a divergence between the robot and the Virtual
Lab becomes a failing test instead of a differing audit record.

## `traces/` — whole runs

Each file is one mission: the task source it was compiled from, the world it ran
against, the run outcome, the compiled IR, and every journal event.

| Fixture | World and scenario | Outcome | Events | `journalHash` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aracnid-nominal-seed7-arc.json` | `AracnidWorld`, nominal, seed 7, arc | completed, exit 0 | 297 | `ca0008e7fbb31f68a1a6df16e1fc4e1630679e418f22e27419bec1dfbfbab90e` |
| `aracnid-nominal-seed7-straight.json` | `AracnidWorld`, nominal, seed 7, straight | completed, exit 0 | 265 | `a0849c689fb3…` |
| `aracnid-tilt-breach-seed7-arc.json` | `AracnidWorld`, tilt breach, seed 7, arc | inhibited, exit 4, `EGGS_ROUND_ABORTED` | 175 | `75044336cc61…` |
| `aracnid-fewer-eggs-seed7-arc.json` | `AracnidWorld`, fewer eggs than hands, seed 7, arc | failed, exit 1, `EGGS_ROUND_ABORTED` | 172 | `7480ffffffe7…` |
| `probe-permit-and-verify.json` | `ScriptedWorld`, three-statement probe task | completed, exit 0 | 31 | `7295129215cc…` |

The four ARACNID runs use the Virtual Lab's own run-id shape
(`lab-aracnid-egg-collection-<scenario>-<seed>-<layout>`), so the nominal fixture
is the same round the lab renders and reproduces the hash `docs/09` quotes. The
tilt-breach run is there because exit 4 reports the *task's* abort code while the
real inhibition — `E_GUARD_BREACH` — is only visible in the journal, which is
exactly the kind of detail a port can lose.

`aracnid-fewer-eggs-seed7-arc.json` and `probe-permit-and-verify.json` also carry
`journal.canonicalTrace` and `ir.canonicalJson`: the canonical bytes themselves,
not only their digests. The C++ suite compares those byte for byte, because two
different writers agreeing on a hash would otherwise go unnoticed until they
disagreed.

Fields in a trace fixture:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `fixtureVersion`, `generator`, `contract` | Which contract this file belongs to |
| `task.source`, `task.name`, `task.version` | The AgriScript text and its identity |
| `world` | The world model and the options it was constructed with |
| `run` | `status`, `exitCode`, `errorCode`, `message`, `elapsedMs`, `visits`, `tally`, `safety` |
| `ir.value`, `ir.irHash`, `ir.sourceHash` | The compiled IR and the digest a signature covers |
| `journal.events`, `journal.journalHash`, `journal.eventCount` | The append-only trace and its digest |

Events keep every field the engine writes, including `schemaVersion`, `runId` and
`monotonicNs`, which the hash projection excludes. That is deliberate: it is what
makes the nine-field projection a rule the C++ engine has to implement rather than
an accident of the fixture's shape.

## `vectors/` — canonicalisation rules

Small, readable, and each one aimed at a specific way to be wrong.

- **`numbers.json`** — 50 numbers, each with its IEEE-754 bit pattern
  (`0x…`), its `JSON.stringify` text, and a one-key document wrapping it. Covers
  `-0`, the exponent thresholds (`1e-7`, `1e+21`, `1e+22`), denormals (`5e-324`),
  `Number.MAX_VALUE`, integers past 2^53, and values whose shortest round-trip
  digits are 17 long. `roundTripsBits` is false for `-0` only, because no JSON
  text can carry the sign of zero.
- **`canonical-json.json`** — 13 raw JSON documents, each with both orders:
  `stringify` (insertion order, as `JSON.stringify` writes it) and `canonical`
  (every key sorted). They cover integer-index hoisting, UTF-16 versus code-point
  key order, all seven escapes, C0 control characters, DEL, U+2028/U+2029, raw
  non-ASCII, and deep nesting. The inputs are stored as **text**, not as parsed
  objects: `JSON.parse` hoists integer-index keys on the way in, so a fixture built
  from parsed objects could never reveal a port that forgot to hoist them.

## Rules

1. Do not edit a file here. Change the generator, run `npm run export:golden`,
   commit the result.
2. A hash change is a review event. If `journalHash` or `irHash` moves, the
   fixtures, `engine/test/test_golden_traces.cpp`, and every document that quotes
   the old value change in the same commit.
3. Fixtures stay deterministic. Nothing here may depend on the wall clock, the
   locale, or the order a directory was read in — the generator uses a fixed epoch
   (`DEFAULT_MISSION_EPOCH_MS`) and a fixed seed, and the drift gate fails if a
   regeneration is not byte-identical.
4. Each file stays well under the 5 MB tracked-file limit `scripts/check-tree.mjs`
   enforces, and Prettier is told to leave this directory alone (`.prettierignore`)
   because reformatting a fixture would break the byte comparison.
